name: Felix Doerpmund
headline: Carbon Dioxide Removal and Biomass | CDTM | UCB

ca.about:
Felix Dörpmund studied Business Administration (Münster School of Business) and Information Systems (WWU Münster). During his studies, he focussed on data analytics and sustainability and participated in international research projects on innovation and design at Stanford.

During and after graduating, Felix gained practical experience in web development, data science, as well as in research on Green IT and decarbonization.

Felix joined the CDTM in June of 2022 and is in charge of the Trend Seminar, the Entrepreneurship Taskforce, and Recruitment. He loves to work on everything sustainability and focuses his research on (nature-based) Carbon Dioxide Removal technologies and what it takes to scale them up and keep the planet inhabitable.
researchFields: Carbon Dioxide Removal Synergies, Potentials, Scaling

summary:
Felix is a doctoral candidate at the geosciences department of the LMU with previous visiting research stints at Stanford and the University of California, Berkeley. Felix' main research focus is on the perception, acceptance, and economics of Carbon Dioxide Removal technologies, specifically biomass-based systems, as well as remote-sensing and gespatial applications. Other research interests include: Geoengineering, translation of science to commercial.

Felix is also part of the management team of the CDTM, one of the most successful entrepreneurship education institutions (per-capita) worldwide.

company.description:
The Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), a joint institution of the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU) and the Technische Universität München (TUM), offers talented students the international and interdisciplinary study program Technology Management. 

The CDTM focuses on how to manage High-Tech in close cooperation with industry, research and education, while simultaneously being committed to preparing the students for future leadership positions in their professional career.
